key_insight: Quantum simulations designed to calculate response functions also prepare many-body states that reveal how information propagates, becomes locally accessible, and supports entanglement-based tasks.
engineering_relevance: Existing response-simulation protocols could support additional quantum-information analyses without redesigning state preparation, though measurement and analysis requirements may differ.
method: Study local-pulse Green-function protocols in finite XX and XXX spin chains.
Encode a classical bit using opposite source rotations and track its propagation and accessibility in local subsystems.
Compare covariance-based reconstruction and spin-measurement readout, then analyze source-angle estimation, Bell-state recovery, communication rates, and entanglement.
evidence_signal: In the studied chains, fermionic covariance data exactly reconstruct the signed XX response, yet simple spin measurements recover a larger fraction of locally available information in XXX; this ordering persists for local source-angle estimation.
watch_item: Results concern finite spin-chain case studies; scalability and robustness to experimental noise are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Dynamical quantum simulations as laboratories for quantum information
